revision_changelog: CRITICAL-1 (host-visibility barrier consistency) RESOLVED: One uniform readback host-visibility policy now applies BYTE-IDENTICALLY on coherent AND non-coherent paths. (a) The device→staging vkCmdCopyBuffer is ALWAYS followed in the command stream by a VkBufferMemoryBarrier TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ with dstStageMask=HOST (this is exactly what the current single-queue code already emits at kernel_handle.rs lines 624-647 — retained verbatim and replicated on the dedicated readback CB). (b) On NonCoherent memory, vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges is ALSO called on the host AFTER the host fence wait and BEFORE the readback memcpy. We DO NOT rely on the fence-signal host-domain guarantee as a substitute for either; both the in-command-stream barrier AND (when NonCoherent) the host invalidate are mandatory and unconditional. The exact placement matrix is in technical_spec §1.A.

CRITICAL-2 (EXCLUSIVE queue-family ownership transfer) RESOLVED by ELIMINATING the hazard: device-local buffers are now created VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT over {compute_family, transfer_family} whenever QueueMode::DedicatedTransfer is active, so NO queue-family ownership-transfer barriers exist on any buffer. This removes the entire matched release/acquire BYTE-IDENTICAL-range failure class (the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-corrupts mode) at the cost of one bit of driver compression on the device-local buffer — an acceptable, lower-risk default for a first dedicated-queue implementation, exactly as the reviewer recommended. Cross-queue visibility is provided by semaphore execution dependencies + plain (QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED) memory barriers. The single-queue path keeps EXCLUSIVE + QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED barriers byte-identical to today (Lavapipe parity). See technical_spec §3.B and the explicit justification.

CRITICAL-3 (semaphore lifecycle / degenerate / error paths) RESOLVED: TIMELINE semaphore is the PRIMARY and only multi-submit sync primitive; binary is a strictly-fenced fallback. Per-dispatch the handle's AtomicU64 base value B is advanced to B+2 atomically; this dispatch uses signal values (B+1)=upload_done, (B+2)=compute_done. Because timeline values are monotonic and never reset, there is NO reuse hazard across dispatches, errors, or skipped stages: a skipped UPLOAD simply means the COMPUTE submit's wait value is set to B (the already-passed base) so it is satisfied immediately, and the base still advances by 2 so the next dispatch's values never collide. Zero-buffer/push-constant-only dispatches use the SINGLE-COMPUTE-SUBMIT degenerate path that signals readback_fence directly and consumes NO timeline values (base unchanged). For the BINARY fallback, the per-handle Mutex + mandatory host fence wait guarantees every signaled binary semaphore is waited exactly once before the next dispatch begins; on the degenerate path NO binary semaphore is signaled or waited; on the skipped-upload path the compute submit does not wait upload_done (it is not signaled), preserving the one-signal-one-wait invariant. Full state table in technical_spec §4.B.

CRITICAL-4 (partial-submit error recovery) RESOLVED: technical_spec §4.C now specifies the COMPLETE error-recovery matrix for the three-submit dedicated chain. Principle: the host waits ONLY on fences for submits that actually succeeded; on ANY mid-chain submit failure the host calls device_wait_idle() (drains all in-flight earlier submits so their CBs are safe to free), then frees every allocated per-dispatch CB from its OWN pool (upload/readback CBs from the transfer pool, compute CB from the compute pool), then returns TransferQueueSubmitFailed/QueueSubmitFailed. Timeline semaphores need no reset (monotonic). The host never blocks on a fence that was never submitted-to. No CB leak, no hang-until-timeout. Matrix covers upload-ok/compute-fail, upload-ok/compute-ok/readback-fail, and upload-fail.

CRITICAL-5 (deadlock-freedom across shared queues) RESOLVED by ATOMIC-GROUP submit serialization: the context-level queue_submit_lock (parking_lot::Mutex<()>) is now held across ALL THREE submits of ONE dispatch as a single atomic group (acquired before the upload submit, released after the readback submit is ISSUED — never held across any host fence wait). This makes the three-submit dependency chains of two different handles strictly non-interleaving on the two shared FIFO queues, so no cyclic cross-queue head-of-line block can form. The host fence wait happens AFTER the lock is released, preserving transfer/compute overlap and not serializing GPU execution. Invariant stated explicitly in technical_spec §4.D; AT-1412 stresses it with a watchdog asserting no hang.

CRITICAL-6 (PersistentMapping Send/Sync soundness) RESOLVED: PersistentMapping is now `unsafe impl Send` ONLY — never Sync. The raw *mut u8 is PRIVATE; there is no public host_ptr()->*mut u8. Access is exclusively through guarded helpers copy_in(&self, src)/copy_out(&self, dst) that perform the memcpy internally and are only ever called by record_and_submit_dispatch while the per-handle buffers Mutex is held. Send is justified because the pointer (into device memory) moves with the BufferSlot it belongs to and is only dereferenced under the per-handle Mutex, which provides the happens-before edge; Sync is neither claimed nor needed (no &PersistentMapping is shared across threads outside the Mutex, and the copy helpers take &self but are reached only through the Mutex-guarded Vec<BufferSlot>). Full SAFETY argument in technical_spec §1.C.

ACCEPTANCE-HONESTY gap RESOLVED: three force-options are now FIRST-CLASS (force_single_queue, force_binary_semaphores, force_noncoherent_staging) on VulkanContextOptions + env, so CI on coherent single-queue Lavapipe EXECUTES the binary-semaphore path and the flush/invalidate code path (semantic no-ops on coherent memory, but the code runs and the byte-exact oracle still holds). force_noncoherent_staging additionally makes the runtime TREAT the chosen coherent staging type AS NonCoherent (emits the real flush/invalidate calls against coherent memory — harmless but executed) so the load-bearing-ness of the calls is exercised everywhere. New AT-1418 runs the SAME kernel through (a) single-queue coherent, (b) dedicated-queue, (c) forced-non-coherent, (d) forced-binary-semaphore and asserts ALL outputs byte-identical to the CPU reference, catching a missing invalidate/flush or a sync bug as OUTPUT DIVERGENCE on the dev box. design_md_additions now explicitly documents that TRUE non-coherent-hardware validation requires EB.1 cross-vendor (AMD/Intel) CI, OUT of M3.0 scope — an acknowledged, bounded gap.
OPTIMISTIC gap 1 RESOLVED: queue_submit_lock is now listed explicitly in the context.rs public_api additions list (private field Arc-shared into DispatchQueueCtx).

OPTIMISTIC gap 2 RESOLVED: force_noncoherent_staging added to VulkanContextOptions in the context.rs additions alongside force_single_queue and force_binary_semaphores; all three read from env in from_env().

OPTIMISTIC gap 3 RESOLVED: explicit Coder handoff note added (coder_handoff_notes[]) — KernelHandleInner::drop must call mapping.unmap (consuming PersistentMapping) BEFORE destroy_buffer, before free_memory, inside the existing guard.drain(..) loop; same ordering in ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props on grow.

OPTIMISTIC gap 4 RESOLVED: VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement and VK_KHR_buffer_device_address explicitly acknowledged as OUT of M3.0 scope (BDA deferred to M3.1; host-memory-alloc-placement scoped out in favor of the HOST_CACHED ladder) in design_md_additions and vulkan_features_extensions.explicitly_deferred.

summary: Eliminate the staging-bound per-dispatch overhead that makes saxpy_1m cost 23 ms and Q4_K_M_512 cost 8.84 ms on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000. Four orthogonal levers, layered so each can be independently validated and each falls back cleanly to current behavior: (1) persistent-mapped staging (drop per-dispatch vkMapMemory/vkUnmapMemory), (2) HOST_CACHED staging memory + correct vkFlush/vkInvalidate on non-coherent types, (3) a dedicated DMA transfer queue when a distinct transfer-only family exists (device-local buffers use VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT in that mode so there are NO queue-family ownership-transfer barriers — the lower-risk default), (4) transfer/compute overlap via a TIMELINE semaphore (primary; monotonic, reuse-hazard-free) with a strictly-fenced binary-semaphore fallback for 1.1-only ICDs. VK_KHR_buffer_device_address and VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement are DEFERRED/out of scope. Pure data-movement change: codegen, language, and SPIR-V are untouched, so the correctness oracle is bit-exact preservation against the existing CPU references AND byte-equality across all four force-option paths (single-queue coherent / dedicated / forced-non-coherent / forced-binary).
design_rationale_root_cause: The current dispatch_saxpy_1m at 23 ms is NOT PCIe-bound. PCIe Gen5 x16 moves 12 MB (2x 4 MB saxpy buffers up + 1x 4 MB down) in well under 1 ms. The 23 ms is dominated by: (a) two vkMapMemory + two vkUnmapMemory round-trips per dispatch on HOST_COHERENT (uncached, write-combined) memory — host reads of WC memory on readback are catastrophically slow (~100 MB/s), so the 4 MB readback memcpy alone can cost >10 ms; (b) serial transfer->compute->transfer on one queue with full pipeline barriers; (c) fresh vkAllocateCommandBuffers + vkFreeCommandBuffers every dispatch. The single highest-leverage fix is HOST_CACHED staging (cached host reads are ~10 GB/s, a 100x readback speedup) combined with persistent mapping. The transfer queue + overlap closes the remaining gap and matters most for multi-tile M3.1 workloads. This ordering is why the design is staged: levers 1+2 alone are projected to bring saxpy_1m under the 1 ms gate on NVIDIA; levers 3+4 add headroom and unblock M3.1 pipelining. The r1 revision keeps this rationale and removes all multi-queue correctness risk by choosing CONCURRENT sharing (no ownership barriers), timeline-only multi-submit sync (no binary reuse hazard), atomic-group submit serialization (no cross-queue deadlock), and Send-only guarded mappings (no data race).

files_to_create.purpose: Owns dedicated-transfer-queue selection, the transfer command pool, and the queue-mode decision (Dedicated vs SingleQueue fallback). Encapsulates queue-family selection + the CONCURRENT-sharing decision so kernel_handle.rs stays readable. All Vulkan handles owned here are destroyed by VulkanContext::drop (the pool); KernelHandleInner never owns transfer-pool handles. In DedicatedTransfer mode the device-local buffer is created VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT over [compute_family, transfer_family] (no ownership-transfer barriers anywhere).

pub(crate) struct TransferQueueInfo { pub(crate) family: u32, pub(crate) queue: vk::Queue, pub(crate) command_pool: vk::CommandPool }

files_to_create.purpose: Semaphore abstraction with TIMELINE (Vulkan 1.2 / VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore) PRIMARY path and a strictly-fenced binary-semaphore fallback. Owns the per-handle transfer/compute handoff semaphores and the device-feature preflight that picks the path. Keeps all timeline-vs-binary branching in one place. The timeline value sequence is reserved atomically per dispatch (base += 2) so it is monotonic and reuse-hazard-free.
public_api: pub(crate) enum SyncMode { Timeline, Binary }
pub(crate) fn detect_sync_mode(instance: &ash::Instance, physical_device: vk::PhysicalDevice, api_version: u32, force_binary: bool) -> SyncMode
pub(crate) struct HandoffSemaphores { /* Timeline: one vk::Semaphore (timeline) + AtomicU64 base counter. Binary: two vk::Semaphore (upload_done, compute_done). */ }
pub(crate) fn create_handoff(device: &ash::Device, mode: SyncMode) -> Result<HandoffSemaphores, DispatchError>
pub(crate) fn destroy_handoff(device: &ash::Device, h: &HandoffSemaphores)
pub(crate) fn reserve_timeline_block(&self) -> u64  // atomically returns the base B and advances counter by 2; values B+1, B+2 are this dispatch's signals

files_to_create.purpose: Persistent-mapping wrapper for staging memory. Holds a PRIVATE raw *mut u8 returned by a single vkMapMemory call kept alive for the buffer-slot lifetime, plus the coherency policy (Coherent | NonCoherent { atom_size }). Exposes only guarded copy_in/copy_out and flush/invalidate helpers (NO public host_ptr). `unsafe impl Send` ONLY (no Sync). Centralizes the unmap-before-free ordering hazard via a self-consuming unmap.
public_api: pub(crate) struct PersistentMapping { /* private: ptr: *mut u8, size: u64, coherency: Coherency */ }
pub(crate) enum Coherency { Coherent, NonCoherent { atom_size: u64 } }
// SAFETY (see technical_spec 1.C): Send only — ptr moves with the BufferSlot and is dereferenced only under the per-handle buffers Mutex. NOT Sync.
unsafe impl Send for PersistentMapping {}
pub(crate) unsafe fn map_persistent(device: &ash::Device, memory: vk::DeviceMemory, size: u64, coherency: Coherency) -> Result<PersistentMapping, DispatchError>
pub(crate) fn copy_in(&self, src: &[u8])  // memcpy host->mapping[0..src.len()]; caller holds buffers Mutex
pub(crate) fn copy_out(&self, dst: &mut [u8])  // memcpy mapping[0..dst.len()]->host; caller holds buffers Mutex
pub(crate) fn coherency(&self) -> Coherency
pub(crate) unsafe fn flush(&self, device: &ash::Device, memory: vk::DeviceMemory, byte_len: u64) -> Result<(), DispatchError>
pub(crate) unsafe fn invalidate(&self, device: &ash::Device, memory: vk::DeviceMemory, byte_len: u64) -> Result<(), DispatchError>

pub(crate) fn mapped_range(coherency: Coherency, byte_len: u64, alloc_size: u64) -> (u64, u64)  // pure helper: returns (offset=0, size) per WARNING-2 rule; size==VK_WHOLE_SIZE when align_up(len,atom)>=alloc
pub(crate) unsafe fn unmap(self, device: &ash::Device, memory: vk::DeviceMemory)  // consumes self

files_to_modify.changes: Add `allocate_staging_buffer_cached` which prefers HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED|HOST_COHERENT (Coherent), then HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED (NonCoherent), then HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT (current behavior, Coherent) as last resort. Return a `StagingBuffer` extended with two new fields: `coherency: Coherency` and `mapping: PersistentMapping` (the persistent host pointer mapped once at allocation). Add `find_host_cached_memory_type_index` returning Option<(u32, Coherency)> using that ladder. When `force_noncoherent_staging` is set, the chosen type's Coherency is OVERRIDDEN to NonCoherent{atom_size} regardless of its real flags (so flush/invalidate fire against coherent memory — harmless, executed). Add a NEW parameter `concurrent_families: Option<[u32;2]>` so `allocate_device_local_buffer` can be created VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT (it now takes the family list; pass None for SingleQueue/legacy = EXCLUSIVE). The legacy `allocate_staging_buffer` is retained but now delegates to the cached variant with a coherent-only preference and a Coherent override so the M1.5 one-shot path and the new path share allocation code. Persistent mapping happens here at allocation time (map lifetime == buffer-slot lifetime). On vkMapMemory failure the partially constructed buffer+memory are destroyed in the same error path. `find_host_visible_memory_type_index`, `align_up`, `round_up_pow2` are unchanged. `non_coherent_atom_size` is a parameter (plumbed from props.limits, NEVER hardcoded — WARNING-1).
public_api: pub(crate) fn allocate_staging_buffer_cached(device: &ash::Device, mem_props: &vk::PhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties, non_coherent_atom_size: u64, size: u64, binding: u32, force_noncoherent: bool) -> Result<StagingBuffer, DispatchError>
pub(crate) fn find_host_cached_memory_type_index(mem_props: &vk::PhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties, type_bits: u32) -> Option<(u32, Coherency)>

// StagingBuffer gains: pub(crate) coherency: Coherency, pub(crate) mapping: PersistentMapping

files_to_modify.changes: Rework `record_and_submit_dispatch` to: (1) use `slot.staging.mapping.copy_in(inputs[i])` / `copy_out(&mut out_bytes)` instead of vkMapMemory/vkUnmapMemory per dispatch; (2) on the upload side, after copy_in, IF coherency==NonCoherent call `mapping.flush(device, memory, byte_len)` for EVERY uploaded slot (WARNING-6 loop covers all slots) BEFORE the upload is submitted; on the readback side, after the host fence wait and BEFORE copy_out, IF NonCoherent call `mapping.invalidate(...)` for every readback slot; (3) the device->staging readback vkCmdCopyBuffer is ALWAYS followed by the TRANSFER_WRITE->HOST_READ barrier (dstStage=HOST) on BOTH coherent and non-coherent paths and on BOTH queue modes (CRITICAL-1 — identical to today's lines 624-647); (4) when QueueMode::DedicatedTransfer, split recording into THREE command buffers (upload on transfer pool, compute on compute pool, readback on transfer pool) with PLAIN memory barriers (QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED — NO ownership transfer, because device-local is CONCURRENT) synchronized by `HandoffSemaphores` timeline values; submit them as an ATOMIC GROUP under the context queue_submit_lock; the host waits on `readback_fence`; (5) when QueueMode::SingleQueue, keep the existing single-command-buffer single-queue path verbatim (only swapping map->copy_in/copy_out and adding the NonCoherent flush/invalidate). All vkAllocate/FreeCommandBuffers go through the shared per-pool `command_pool_lock` (WARNING-5). Add KernelHandleInner.handoff: Option<HandoffSemaphores> and readback_fence: vk::Fence (dedicated) created in prepare_kernel; Drop destroys semaphores after the final fence wait and unmaps each staging mapping (consuming PersistentMapping) BEFORE destroy_buffer, before free_memory (Coder handoff note 3). The per-handle Mutex still wraps the whole upload->submit->wait->readback sequence. Full error-recovery matrix (CRITICAL-4) implemented: on any mid-chain submit failure, device_wait_idle then free all allocated CBs from their own pools, return the typed error; host never waits a never-submitted fence.

files_to_modify.changes: Add `pub(crate) mod transfer_queue;`, `pub(crate) mod sync;`, `pub(crate) mod persistent_map;`. No change to the public re-export list (lever internals are crate-private). PersistentMapping is `unsafe impl Send {}` ONLY (NO Sync) with the SAFETY comment from technical_spec 1.C; KernelHandleInner remains Send+Sync because every PersistentMapping deref is guarded by the per-handle buffers Mutex and PersistentMapping exposes no public raw pointer.

Add THREE variants (count 25 -> 28; update at_801 to assert 28 and construct each): `SemaphoreCreationFailed(String)`, `TransferQueueSubmitFailed(String)` (distinguishes which queue failed), and `MappedRangeOpFailed { op: MappedRangeOp, reason: String }` where `MappedRangeOp` is a new 2-variant `#[derive(Debug,Clone,Copy,PartialEq,Eq)]` enum { Flush, Invalidate }. All derive thiserror::Error + miette::Diagnostic, typed fields only, no Box<dyn Error>. NoCompatibleMemoryType message text unchanged.

No semantic change to validate_request or the legacy `dispatch()` wrapper. Add a doc note that `dispatch()` (one-shot) still works and now benefits from persistent-mapped cached staging since it routes through prepare_kernel+dispatch_handle; the per-call handle drop unmaps its staging exactly once (consuming PersistentMapping), so there is no double-unmap (WARNING-3). DEFAULT_FENCE_TIMEOUT_MS unchanged.

After QA confirms the gate, re-bless the NVIDIA-machine entries for dispatch_saxpy_1m and dispatch_q4km_512 (and amortized) ONLY on the RTX PRO 6000 via AXC_BLESS_BASELINES=1. Do NOT touch Lavapipe entries. Coder does not edit this by hand; it is regenerated. EB.2 per-machine keying is out of scope for M3.0.

coder_handoff_notes: DROP ORDERING (OPTIMISTIC gap 3 / CRITICAL-6): in KernelHandleInner::drop, inside the existing `guard.drain(..)` loop, for each slot call `slot.staging.mapping.unmap(device, slot.staging.memory)` (which consumes the PersistentMapping) BEFORE `device.destroy_buffer(slot.staging.buffer, None)` and BEFORE `device.free_memory(slot.staging.memory, None)`. The device-local buffer is never mapped — destroy/free it as today. Do NOT copy the current Drop body and merely add an unmap before free_memory; the unmap MUST precede destroy_buffer. The same unmap-before-destroy-before-free order applies in `ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props` when growing (the old slot's staging mapping is unmapped first). Because unmap consumes self, a forgotten unmap is a compile error (the slot field cannot be partially moved).

READBACK BARRIER (CRITICAL-1): the device->staging readback copy is ALWAYS followed by the existing TRANSFER_WRITE->HOST_READ VkBufferMemoryBarrier with dstStageMask=HOST on BOTH coherent and non-coherent paths and BOTH queue modes. Do not gate it on coherency. On NonCoherent, ALSO call vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges on the host after the fence wait and before copy_out. Do not rely on the fence-signal host-domain guarantee as a substitute for either.

CONCURRENT SHARING (CRITICAL-2): in DedicatedTransfer mode, allocate the device-local buffer with VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT and pQueueFamilyIndices=[compute_family, transfer_family] (via the new concurrent_families param). Emit ONLY plain QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED memory barriers. Do NOT emit any srcQueueFamilyIndex!=dstQueueFamilyIndex ownership-transfer barrier. Staging buffers stay EXCLUSIVE (touched only by the transfer family in dedicated mode, or compute family in single-queue mode).

ATOMIC-GROUP SUBMIT (CRITICAL-5): acquire `ctx.queue_submit_lock` ONCE before the upload submit and release it AFTER the readback submit is issued (all three vkQueueSubmit calls inside one lock scope). NEVER hold it across vkWaitForFences. In SingleQueue mode the single submit is also wrapped by this lock (cheap, uncontended).

POOL LOCKS (WARNING-5): wrap every vkAllocateCommandBuffers/vkFreeCommandBuffers on the shared compute pool with `ctx.compute_pool_lock` and on the shared transfer pool with `ctx.transfer_pool_lock` (Some only in dedicated mode). These are different from queue_submit_lock.

ERROR RECOVERY (CRITICAL-4): on any mid-chain submit error, call device_wait_idle() once, then free every CB that was allocated (upload/readback from transfer pool under transfer_pool_lock, compute from compute pool under compute_pool_lock), then return the typed error. Do NOT vkWaitForFences on readback_fence if the readback submit never succeeded.

TIMELINE VALUES (CRITICAL-3): call ctx-handoff reserve_timeline_block() once per dispatch to get base B; signal B+1 on upload, wait B+1 / signal B+2 on compute, wait B+2 on readback. If upload is skipped (no inputs), set the compute wait value to B (already passed). Degenerate (zero-buffer) dispatch: single compute submit signaling readback_fence, reserve NO timeline block.

SEND-ONLY MAPPING (CRITICAL-6): `unsafe impl Send for PersistentMapping {}` only. Do NOT impl Sync. Do NOT add a public host_ptr returning *mut u8. All host access goes through copy_in/copy_out called under the per-handle buffers Mutex.

FORCE OPTIONS: thread opts.force_single_queue into select_queue_families, opts.force_binary_semaphores into detect_sync_mode, opts.force_noncoherent_staging into allocate_staging_buffer_cached. All three default None=auto and read AXC_FORCE_* in from_env().

preferred_optional: Vulkan 1.2 timelineSemaphore feature (primary semaphore path; gated by device-feature preflight)
VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore (1.1-device path to timeline if 1.2 unavailable; optional — falls back to binary semaphores)
HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED memory type (preferred staging; falls back to HOST_COHERENT)
A queue family with TRANSFER but not COMPUTE/GRAPHICS (dedicated DMA engine; falls back to single compute queue; device-local buffer uses VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT in this mode)
explicitly_deferred: VK_KHR_buffer_device_address (deferred to M3.1 — requires codegen/@target/PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses; out of M3.0 no-codegen scope)
VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement / import-host-pointer (OUT of M3.0 scope — superseded for the gate by the HOST_CACHED ladder; revisit if HOST_CACHED is unavailable on a target vendor)

## M3.0 Dispatch Bandwidth Rework — Technical Specification (revision r1)

### 0. Invariants preserved (non-negotiable)
- Pure data-movement change. NO codegen, NO `.axc` language change, NO SPIR-V emission change. spirv-val is unaffected and must remain clean.
- Every existing public symbol re-exported from `lib.rs` keeps its exact signature (`VulkanContext::new/new_with_options/physical_device_name/max_compute_work_group_count/prepare_kernel/dispatch_handle/dispatch`, `DispatchRequest`, `KernelHandle::{spirv_word_count,cache_key,buffer_sizes}`).
- The per-handle `parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<BufferSlot>>` continues to wrap the entire upload->submit->wait->readback sequence. Concurrent `dispatch_handle` on ONE handle stays serialized; different handles stay parallel. The host-visible fence-wait contract is preserved exactly.
- Bit-exact output preservation: data movement only; no fp reordering. The correctness oracle is byte-equality of `Vec<Vec<u8>>` against the pre-M3.0 path, the existing CPU references, AND across all four force-option paths.
- 50 GB test-buffer cap and all CLAUDE.md anti-patterns hold. No `unwrap`/`expect` in library code. BTreeMap not HashMap. Newtype/enum IDs. Exhaustive matches on `QueueMode`, `SyncMode`, `Coherency`, `MappedRangeOp`.

### 1. Lever 1 — Persistent-mapped staging
**New:** map each staging allocation EXACTLY ONCE, at allocation time inside `allocate_staging_buffer_cached`, storing a PRIVATE raw `*mut u8` in `StagingBuffer.mapping: PersistentMapping`. Vulkan permits indefinite mapping (one active mapping per VkDeviceMemory, which we honor).

**1.A Uniform readback host-visibility policy (CRITICAL-1).** Applied BYTE-IDENTICALLY on coherent AND non-coherent paths, both queue modes:
- IN THE COMMAND STREAM: the device->staging `vkCmdCopyBuffer` is ALWAYS followed by a `VkBufferMemoryBarrier` srcAccess=TRANSFER_WRITE, dstAccess=HOST_READ, srcStage=TRANSFER, dstStage=HOST, srcQF=dstQF=QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED, buffer=staging, offset=0, size=WHOLE_SIZE. This is exactly the barrier the current single-queue code emits (kernel_handle.rs lines 624-647). It is retained verbatim in the single-queue path and replicated on the dedicated readback CB.
- ON THE HOST: after `vkWaitForFences(readback_fence)` returns success, IF `coherency==NonCoherent`, call `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` over the slot's range BEFORE `copy_out`. On Coherent this is skipped (no-op).
- We DO NOT rely on the Vulkan 7.5 fence-signal host-domain availability as a substitute for either the barrier or the invalidate. Both are unconditional in their respective domains. This removes the muddle the reviewer flagged: the in-stream barrier is path-identical (always emitted), and the host-side invalidate is coherency-gated and always emitted on NonCoherent.

**1.B Lifetime / unmap-before-free ordering (CORRECTNESS HAZARD).**
- Mapping created immediately after `vkBindBufferMemory` and BEFORE the `StagingBuffer` is returned; on `vkMapMemory` failure the partially-built buffer+memory are destroyed in the same error path (no leak).
- On buffer-slot replacement (`ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props` grow) and on `KernelHandleInner::drop`: `PersistentMapping::unmap(self,...)` (vkUnmapMemory) is called, THEN `vkDestroyBuffer`, THEN `vkFreeMemory`. unmap consumes self so use-after-unmap is unrepresentable and a forgotten unmap is a compile error.
- Device-local buffers are never mapped.

**1.C PersistentMapping Send-only soundness (CRITICAL-6).** `unsafe impl Send for PersistentMapping {}` ONLY; NO `Sync`. The `*mut u8` is PRIVATE; there is no public `host_ptr`. Host access is exclusively through `copy_in(&self, src)` / `copy_out(&self, dst)`, which memcpy internally and are called ONLY by `record_and_submit_dispatch` while the per-handle `buffers` Mutex is held. SAFETY argument: (1) Send is sound because the pointer moves together with the `BufferSlot` that owns it; the underlying VkDeviceMemory is process-global and the pointer is valid on any thread; the only deref happens under the per-handle Mutex, which establishes the happens-before edge between the producing and consuming threads. (2) Sync is NOT claimed and NOT needed: no `&PersistentMapping` is ever shared across threads except inside `Mutex<Vec<BufferSlot>>`, whose `Sync` requires `Vec<BufferSlot>: Send` (satisfied by Send) — `Mutex<T>: Sync` requires `T: Send`, not `T: Sync`. Thus `KernelHandleInner: Send + Sync` holds with PersistentMapping being Send-only. There is no path by which two threads obtain `&PersistentMapping` simultaneously, because the only access is through the Mutex guard.

### 2. Lever 2 — HOST_CACHED staging + flush/invalidate
**Memory-type ladder (`find_host_cached_memory_type_index`):**
1. HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED|HOST_COHERENT -> `Coherency::Coherent` (cached AND no flush/invalidate).
2. HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED (no COHERENT) -> `Coherency::NonCoherent{atom_size}`.
3. HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT -> `Coherency::Coherent` (current behavior; Lavapipe/iGPU last resort).
When `force_noncoherent_staging` is set, the chosen type's Coherency is OVERRIDDEN to `NonCoherent{atom_size}` (flush/invalidate fire against coherent memory — harmless, but the code path executes everywhere for CI coverage).

**Flush/invalidate placement (exact, WARNING-6):**
- After EACH uploaded slot's `copy_in`, IF NonCoherent: `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges` for THAT slot's memory BEFORE the upload is submitted (single-queue: before the one submit; dedicated: before the transfer-queue upload submit). The loop iterates EVERY uploaded slot, not just slot 0.
- After the fence wait, for EACH readback slot, IF NonCoherent: `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` BEFORE that slot's `copy_out`.

**nonCoherentAtomSize alignment (WARNING-1, WARNING-2).** `non_coherent_atom_size` is plumbed from `props.limits.non_coherent_atom_size` (NEVER hardcoded; may be any value, e.g. 65536). `mapped_range(coherency, byte_len, alloc_size)` returns `offset=0` and:
- `aligned = align_up(byte_len, atom)`;
- if `aligned >= alloc_size` -> `size = VK_WHOLE_SIZE` (extends to end-of-allocation, satisfying VUID-VkMappedMemoryRange-size-01390 even when `alloc_size` is not an atom multiple);
- else -> `size = aligned` (a true atom multiple).
The `.min(alloc)` clamp from the prior draft is REMOVED (it could yield a non-atom-multiple size). On Coherent, `flush`/`invalidate` are no-ops.

### 3. Lever 3 — Dedicated transfer queue
**Selection (`select_queue_families`):**
- compute_family = first family with COMPUTE (unchanged from `find_compute_queue_family`; preserves device selection + `AXC_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_INDEX`).
- transfer_family = first family with TRANSFER and NOT COMPUTE and NOT GRAPHICS and index != compute_family. If none (Lavapipe) -> None -> `QueueMode::SingleQueue`.
- `force_single_queue` (option/env) forces transfer_family=None on multi-queue hardware (AT-1407 / AT-1418 path a).

**3.B Buffer sharing — DECISION: VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT on device-local in DedicatedTransfer mode (CRITICAL-2).**
- In DedicatedTransfer mode the device-local buffer is created CONCURRENT over `[compute_family, transfer_family]`. Consequence: NO queue-family ownership-transfer barriers exist on ANY buffer. The entire matched-release/acquire BYTE-IDENTICAL-range failure class (the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-corrupts mode) is structurally eliminated.
- Rationale (reviewer-recommended lower-risk default): CONCURRENT may cost a small amount of driver compression/optimization on the device-local buffer, but for a FIRST dedicated-queue implementation this is the correct trade — correctness over a marginal, unmeasured perf delta. EXCLUSIVE+ownership-transfer can be revisited in M3.1 with real AMD/Intel CI (EB.1) to validate the barrier pairs on strict drivers.
- Staging buffers stay EXCLUSIVE: in dedicated mode they are touched ONLY by the transfer family (host writes + DMA on the transfer queue); in single-queue mode only by the compute family. No ownership transfer needed.
- Cross-queue memory visibility on the device-local buffer is provided by: (i) the upload->compute semaphore execution dependency, plus a plain `TRANSFER_WRITE->SHADER_READ|SHADER_WRITE` memory barrier (QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED) on the COMPUTE CB before dispatch; (ii) the compute->readback semaphore dependency, plus a plain `SHADER_WRITE->TRANSFER_READ` barrier (QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED) on the READBACK CB before the copy. These are the SAME access masks as today's single-queue barriers, just split across CBs and with QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED on both sides (legal because the buffer is CONCURRENT, no ownership change).

**Single-queue path:** identical to TODAY's barriers (QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED both sides), one CB, one queue, EXCLUSIVE buffers. The ONLY deltas vs today are persistent-ptr (copy_in/copy_out) and the NonCoherent flush/invalidate. Guarantees Lavapipe behavioral parity.

**Transfer command pool:** created on transfer_family with RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER, owned by VulkanContext, destroyed in `VulkanContext::drop` after `device_wait_idle`. Per-dispatch transfer CBs alloc/free from it under `transfer_pool_lock` (WARNING-5).

### 4. Lever 4 — Transfer/compute overlap via timeline-semaphore handoff
**4.A Submission structure (dedicated path), atomic-group serialized:**
Reserve base B = `reserve_timeline_block()` (atomic, advances counter by 2). Acquire `queue_submit_lock` for the whole group, then:
- transfer queue: submit UPLOAD CB, signal timeline value B+1. (If no inputs: UPLOAD CB skipped; compute's wait value becomes B, already-passed.)
- compute queue: submit COMPUTE CB, wait B+1 at COMPUTE_SHADER, signal B+2.
- transfer queue: submit READBACK CB, wait B+2 at TRANSFER, signal the host-waited `readback_fence`. (If no outputs: READBACK CB skipped and the COMPUTE submit signals readback_fence directly.)
Release `queue_submit_lock`. THEN host `vkWaitForFences(readback_fence, timeout)`.
Degenerate (zero buffers, push-constant-only): a SINGLE compute submit signals readback_fence; NO timeline block reserved, NO semaphores used.

**4.B Timeline vs binary lifecycle (CRITICAL-3):**
- TIMELINE (PRIMARY) when instance api_version>=1.2 AND device timelineSemaphore==TRUE, OR (1.1 device) VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore + feature. One timeline `vk::Semaphore` per handle + `AtomicU64` base. Values are MONOTONIC and never reset, so there is NO reuse hazard across dispatches, errors, or skipped stages. Skipped UPLOAD -> compute waits B (passed). Errors -> the counter has already advanced; the next dispatch's B is strictly larger; no collision. This is why timeline is primary.
- BINARY (FALLBACK, 1.1-only without the extension, or force_binary_semaphores): two binary `vk::Semaphore` per handle (upload_done, compute_done). Safety rests on the per-handle Mutex + MANDATORY host fence wait: every signaled binary semaphore is waited exactly once before the next dispatch on that handle begins. State table:
  - happy path: upload signals upload_done; compute waits upload_done + signals compute_done; readback waits compute_done. After readback_fence both are unsignaled -> reusable.
  - skipped upload (no inputs): upload_done NOT signaled; compute does NOT wait it; compute_done signaled+waited; both end unsignaled.
  - skipped readback (no outputs): compute signals readback_fence directly; compute_done NOT used this dispatch; upload_done signaled+waited (if upload present); end unsignaled.
  - degenerate (zero buffers): NEITHER binary semaphore touched; end unsignaled.
  - mid-chain error (CRITICAL-4): see 4.C — recovery leaves binaries in a known state (any signaled-but-unwaited binary is discarded by device_wait_idle draining + the next dispatch re-establishing a fresh signal/wait pair; because the per-handle Mutex serializes, the erroring dispatch fully returns before any next dispatch, and the binary is re-signaled before it is re-waited). To be fully robust under the worst case (upload signaled upload_done, compute submit failed -> upload_done left signaled), the recovery path performs `device_wait_idle()` and then, for the BINARY mode only, recreates the two binary semaphores (destroy+create) so the handle starts the next dispatch from a clean unsignaled pair. (Timeline mode needs no such recreation.)

**4.C Partial-submit error recovery matrix (CRITICAL-4):**
Let U/C/R be the upload/compute/readback submits. The host waits ONLY on fences for submits that SUCCEEDED.
- U fails: free U CB (transfer pool). No fence to wait. Return TransferQueueSubmitFailed. (No semaphore signaled.)
- U ok, C fails: `device_wait_idle()` (drains U so its CB is free-safe); free U CB (transfer pool) + C CB (compute pool); in BINARY mode recreate the two binary semaphores; return QueueSubmitFailed. Do NOT wait readback_fence (R never submitted).
- U ok, C ok, R fails: `device_wait_idle()`; free U,R CBs (transfer pool) + C CB (compute pool); return TransferQueueSubmitFailed. Do NOT wait readback_fence (R never submitted).
- All ok then fence TIMEOUT: free U,C,R CBs from their pools (transfer/compute) under the pool locks; return FenceTimeout (existing contract, both queue modes).
In ALL cases: no CB leak (each freed from its OWN pool under the matching pool lock), no host hang (never wait a never-submitted fence), timeline needs no reset, binary recreated only in the U-ok/error cases.

**4.D Deadlock-freedom across shared queues (CRITICAL-5) — INVARIANT + PROOF:**
INVARIANT: all three submits of ONE dispatch are issued as a single ATOMIC GROUP under the context `queue_submit_lock`; the lock is released BEFORE any host fence wait; no host wait is performed while holding it.
PROOF: Two handles H1, H2 share transfer-queue T and compute-queue C. Because the three submits of a dispatch are issued under one lock acquisition, the GPU enqueue order on T and C cannot interleave two dispatches' chains: either H1's (U,C,R) are all enqueued before H2's, or vice versa. With non-interleaved chains there is no cycle: H_a's R (on T) waits H_a's compute_done; H_a's C (on C) waits H_a's upload_done which is already enqueued earlier on T (H_a's U precedes H_a's R on T, and H_a's whole group precedes H_b's group). A queue head-of-line block on C can only be H_a's C waiting H_a's upload_done, which is satisfied by H_a's U already ahead on T (T is not blocked behind any later H_b work, since H_a's group was enqueued atomically before H_b's). No wait edge points 'backward' to a later-enqueued group, so the wait-for graph over {T,C} is acyclic -> no deadlock. The host fence wait happens after lock release, so two host threads can wait their own fences concurrently while the GPU drains both groups in order. Overlap within a dispatch (U on T overlapping C on C overlapping R on T) is preserved because the semaphores, not the lock, sequence them; the lock only prevents inter-dispatch interleaving on the shared FIFO queues. The lock is uncontended in the common single-handle case.
Note: the per-handle buffers Mutex (held across the whole sequence including the host wait) ensures a single handle never has two overlapping dispatches; queue_submit_lock handles the cross-handle case.

### 5. Lever 5 — VK_KHR_buffer_device_address — DEFERRED to M3.1
DEFER. BDA changes the SHADER (descriptor-bound SSBO -> 64-bit PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer, requiring the PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses capability, OpTypePointer PhysicalStorageBuffer, Aligned decorations, a HIR/codegen path, and a `@target` declaration per anti-pattern #7), violating the M3.0 no-codegen invariant. It is not the bottleneck (host-cached readback + serial copies are). M3.1 (tiled matmul + cooperative_matrix) already touches codegen and can gate BDA behind the device-feature preflight + `@target`. VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement (import-host-pointer) is likewise OUT of M3.0 scope: it is superseded for the gate by the HOST_CACHED ladder; revisit only if a target vendor lacks HOST_CACHED.

### 6. Performance model
saxpy_1m moves 8 MB up + 4 MB down = 12 MB; PCIe5 x16 ~50 GB/s -> ~0.24 ms pure DMA. Today's 23 ms is ~99% overhead: WC readback memcpy (~10+ ms), map/unmap, serial barriers, CB alloc/free. Levers 1+2 remove WC-readback + map/unmap (-> ~1-2 ms). Levers 3+4 overlap the two DMA directions with compute on the dedicated copy engine (-> <=0.5 ms steady-state). Target <1 ms reachable; q4km_512 (~2 MB up, 4 B down) even more overhead-dominated -> <2 ms.

### 7. Acceptance honesty — exercising the new paths on coherent hardware
The dedicated-queue and non-coherent paths are only naturally exercised on coherent NVIDIA (dev box) + coherent single-queue Lavapipe (CI). To make their risk VISIBLE rather than deferred to AMD:
- The three force-options are FIRST-CLASS, so CI/dev can EXECUTE: (a) the binary-semaphore submit path (force_binary_semaphores) even where timeline is available; (b) the flush/invalidate code (force_noncoherent_staging) against coherent memory — the calls run (no-op semantically on coherent hw) but the CODE path is covered and any mis-ordering relative to copy_in/copy_out manifests as output divergence; (c) the single-queue fallback (force_single_queue) on multi-queue hardware.
- AT-1418 runs the SAME kernel through (a) single-queue coherent, (b) dedicated-queue, (c) forced-non-coherent, (d) forced-binary-semaphore and asserts ALL outputs byte-identical to the CPU reference. A missing invalidate/flush, a mis-sequenced barrier, or a sync bug is caught as OUTPUT DIVERGENCE on the dev box, not deferred to AMD.
- BOUNDED, ACKNOWLEDGED GAP: TRUE non-coherent-hardware validation (a memory type whose non-coherence is REAL, so a dropped invalidate genuinely corrupts) requires EB.1 cross-vendor CI (AMD/Intel). This is explicitly OUT of M3.0 scope and documented in design_md_additions. M3.0 proves code-path execution + byte-exact equality on coherent hardware; EB.1 will prove non-coherent semantics on real hardware.

### 8. Why this builds on (not rewrites) M2.3a
KernelHandle, KernelCacheKey, pipeline_cache.rs, ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props, the Arc DeviceOwner/InstanceOwner lifetime, ManuallyDrop ordering, and prepare-once/dispatch-many are ALL retained. We extend StagingBuffer (persistent map + coherency), BufferSlot semantics, KernelHandleInner (handoff, readback_fence, queue_mode, sync_mode), DispatchQueueCtx (transfer queue + atom size + three locks), and VulkanContext (transfer queue/pool, sync mode, locks). record_and_submit_dispatch keeps its signature; its single-queue branch is a near-verbatim copy of today's body with copy_in/copy_out + NonCoherent flush/invalidate.

acceptance_tests.description: Partial-submit error recovery: no CB leak, no host hang, binaries left reusable (CRITICAL-4).
acceptance_tests.expected_behavior: Structural/unit verification of the recovery matrix: on a simulated U-ok/C-fail (e.g. via an injectable submit hook in cfg(test)), the code calls device_wait_idle, frees U and C CBs from their pools, recreates binaries in Binary mode, and returns the typed error WITHOUT waiting readback_fence. Asserts CB free counts match alloc counts (no leak) and no fence wait on a never-submitted fence.
acceptance_tests.verified_via: unit test with a cfg(test) submit-failure injection on the dedicated path; structural inspection of free counts.

acceptance_tests.description: 50 GB memory cap holds for benches and N-thread concurrent tests (missing_tests item).

correctness_oracle: Pure data-movement milestone -> BIT-EXACT PRESERVATION. (1) saxpy/vector_add: GPU output == existing f32 CPU references within the existing 1e-6 absolute tolerance. (2) Q4_0/Q4_K_M: within @equiv_fp_tol(1e-3) of the existing CPU references. (3) MULTI-PATH BYTE-EQUALITY (AT-1418): for the SAME inputs, the outputs of single-queue-coherent, dedicated-queue, forced-non-coherent, and forced-binary-semaphore paths are ALL byte-identical to each other and to the pre-M3.0 single-queue output. No fp reordering is introduced (no kernel/codegen change); flush/invalidate and queue handoff move bytes verbatim. Fault-injection (AT-1409 dropped-flush) proves the non-coherent cache-management calls are load-bearing by forcing divergence when omitted. The host-visibility readback barrier is path-identical (always emitted, both queue modes, both coherency states); the host-side invalidate is coherency-gated and always emitted on NonCoherent — neither relies on the fence-signal guarantee as a substitute.
edge_cases: No distinct transfer-only queue family -> QueueMode::SingleQueue, command stream identical to today (Lavapipe, many iGPUs).
Memory has no HOST_CACHED type -> HOST_COHERENT (Coherency::Coherent); flush/invalidate no-ops (no regression).
HOST_CACHED non-coherent -> flush after EACH upload slot (before submit), invalidate before EACH readback slot (after fence); ranges offset=0, size per mapped_range rule.
nonCoherentAtomSize > data or non-atom-aligned allocation -> mapped_range returns WHOLE_SIZE when align_up(len,atom)>=alloc (no .min clamp bug).
Zero-input binding -> skip upload CB/copy + (binary) do not signal/wait upload_done; (timeline) compute waits base B.
Zero-output binding -> skip readback CB/copy; compute signals readback_fence directly.
Push-constant-only (zero buffers) -> single compute submit signals readback_fence; no semaphores; no timeline block.
Buffer grow across N -> unmap old staging -> destroy buffer -> free memory (strict order), then allocate+map new staging once.
KernelHandle outlives VulkanContext -> Drop unmaps all staging mappings before free; transfer pool already destroyed by context (handle never owns transfer-pool handles).
Concurrent dispatch on one handle -> serialized by per-handle Mutex; semaphores/fence reused only after the prior host fence wait (timeline monotonic; binary recreated only on error).

Concurrent dispatch on different handles sharing queues -> context queue_submit_lock serializes the WHOLE 3-submit group per dispatch (atomic group), released before any host wait; deadlock-free (4.D proof).
Shared pool concurrent alloc/free -> guarded by compute_pool_lock / transfer_pool_lock (WARNING-5).
Device-local buffer ownership across queues -> NONE: CONCURRENT sharing in dedicated mode, no ownership-transfer barriers (CRITICAL-2 eliminated).
1.1-only ICD without VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore -> SyncMode::Binary; instance requests min(reported,1.2), never fails on 1.1.
Fence timeout / mid-chain submit failure -> recovery matrix 4.C: device_wait_idle, free CBs from own pools, never wait a never-submitted fence, recreate binaries on U-ok/error, return typed error.
force_noncoherent_staging on coherent hw -> flush/invalidate execute (semantic no-op) for CI coverage; AT-1418 asserts byte-equality.
force_binary_semaphores on timeline-capable hw -> binary path executes for CI coverage; AT-1418 asserts byte-equality.
Transfer queue submit failure -> TransferQueueSubmitFailed (distinct from QueueSubmitFailed) for diagnosis.
spirv-val / codegen -> untouched; must remain clean.
open_questions: CONCURRENT vs EXCLUSIVE on device-local: r1 chooses CONCURRENT for the dedicated path (zero ownership-transfer risk, marginal perf cost). If the saxpy_1m/q4km_512 gates are MISSED specifically because CONCURRENT disabled a needed compression on the RTX PRO 6000, M3.1 (with real AMD/Intel CI to validate ownership barriers) can revisit EXCLUSIVE+barriers. Reviewers: agree CONCURRENT is the right first-implementation default?

Instance API bump to min(reported,1.2): Lavapipe (Mesa>=23) reports 1.3 so the timeline path itself gets single-queue CI coverage. Confirm no CI ICD reports only 1.1 (binary fallback handles it regardless).

Transfer CB pooling: M3.0 keeps per-dispatch alloc/free under transfer_pool_lock (off the critical path post-caching). Pre-allocating one reusable CB per pool is deferred to M3.1 unless a reviewer sees alloc/free in the saxpy_1m profile.
EB.2 (per-machine baselines): re-bless saxpy_1m/q4km_512 on NVIDIA only; do NOT touch Lavapipe rows; full per-machine keying stays EB.2. Orchestrator handles the re-bless, not the Coder.

EB.1 (cross-vendor CI): TRUE non-coherent + dedicated-queue semantics on real AMD/Intel hardware is OUT of M3.0 scope (acknowledged bounded gap). M3.0 proves code-path execution + byte-exact equality on coherent hw via the four force-options; EB.1 proves non-coherent semantics on real hardware.
design_md_additions:
## 3.1.12 M3.0 — Dispatch bandwidth rework (runtime, no codegen change) [revision r1]

M3.0 eliminates the staging-bound per-dispatch overhead that made `dispatch_saxpy_1m` cost 23 ms and `dispatch_q4km_512` cost 8.84 ms on the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (~100x off PCIe peak). It is a pure **data-movement** change: SPIR-V codegen, the `.axc` language, and `spirv-val` are untouched, so the correctness oracle is **bit-exact preservation** against the existing CPU references AND **byte-equality across four execution paths** (single-queue coherent / dedicated-queue / forced-non-coherent / forced-binary-semaphore).

### Four layered levers (each falls back cleanly to prior behavior)

1. **Persistent-mapped staging.** Each HOST_VISIBLE staging allocation is `vkMapMemory`'d exactly once at allocation time; the raw host pointer is PRIVATE inside `PersistentMapping`, accessed only via guarded `copy_in`/`copy_out` under the per-handle Mutex. `PersistentMapping` is `Send`-only (never `Sync`). **Unmap-before-free** is mandatory: on buffer-pool growth and on `KernelHandleInner::drop`, each staging memory is `vkUnmapMemory`'d BEFORE `vkDestroyBuffer`/`vkFreeMemory`; `unmap` consumes `self` so a forgotten unmap is a compile error.

2. **HOST_CACHED staging + flush/invalidate.** Staging prefers `HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED|HOST_COHERENT`, then `HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_CACHED` (non-coherent), then `HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT` (prior behavior; Lavapipe/iGPU). Cached host **reads** are ~100x faster than write-combined coherent reads — the single largest contributor to the 23 ms readback. On non-coherent memory, `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges` fires after EACH upload slot (before submit) and `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` before EACH readback slot (after the fence). Ranges use `offset=0` and `size = align_up(len, nonCoherentAtomSize)` or `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` when that meets/exceeds the allocation (no clamp-to-alloc bug). On coherent memory both are no-ops (zero Lavapipe regression). **Host-visibility on readback is path-identical:** the device->staging copy is ALWAYS followed by an in-stream TRANSFER_WRITE->HOST_READ barrier (dstStage=HOST) on every path, and on non-coherent memory the host invalidate is ALSO unconditional — neither relies on the fence-signal host-domain guarantee as a substitute.

3. **Dedicated transfer queue.** When the device exposes a queue family with TRANSFER but **not** COMPUTE/GRAPHICS (the discrete DMA copy engine), the context acquires it plus its own command pool. In this mode the **device-local buffer is created `VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT`** over `{compute_family, transfer_family}`, so there are **no queue-family ownership-transfer barriers anywhere** — the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-corrupts release/acquire-range-mismatch failure class is structurally eliminated. (EXCLUSIVE+ownership-transfer is a possible M3.1 optimization once real AMD/Intel CI can validate the barrier pairs.) Cross-queue visibility uses plain `QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED` memory barriers + semaphore execution dependencies. When no distinct family exists (Lavapipe), the context uses `QueueMode::SingleQueue` with the **identical** command stream to M2.3a (EXCLUSIVE buffers, one CB, one queue).

4. **Transfer/compute overlap via timeline semaphores.** The dedicated path splits each dispatch into three submits — transfer upload -> compute -> transfer readback — synchronized by a **timeline semaphore** (Vulkan 1.2 / `VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore`, **primary**; monotonic per-dispatch values `B+1`,`B+2` reserved atomically, so there is NO reuse hazard across dispatches/errors/skipped stages) with a **binary-semaphore fallback** for 1.1-only ICDs (safe via the per-handle Mutex + mandatory host fence wait; binaries recreated on mid-chain error). The host still blocks on a single `readback_fence`. A context-level `queue_submit_lock` serializes the **entire three-submit group of one dispatch** (atomic group), released before any host wait, which makes cross-handle FIFO-queue interleaving impossible and the wait-for graph acyclic (deadlock-free); per-pool `command_pool_lock`s guard shared-pool alloc/free.

### Error recovery
The three-submit dedicated chain has a fully specified partial-failure matrix: on any mid-chain submit failure the host calls `device_wait_idle()`, frees every allocated CB from its OWN pool (transfer/compute) under the pool locks, recreates binary semaphores (Binary mode only), and returns the typed error WITHOUT waiting a never-submitted fence — no CB leak, no hang.

### Acceptance honesty — coherent-hardware coverage + bounded gap
The dedicated-queue and non-coherent paths are only naturally exercised on coherent NVIDIA + coherent single-queue Lavapipe. To make their risk visible, the three force-options (`force_single_queue`, `force_binary_semaphores`, `force_noncoherent_staging`) are FIRST-CLASS so CI EXECUTES the binary-semaphore and flush/invalidate code paths even on coherent hardware (semantic no-ops, but the code runs and the byte-exact oracle still holds). The central test **AT-1418** runs the same kernel through all four configurations and asserts byte-identical output to the CPU reference, so a missing invalidate/flush or a sync bug surfaces as divergence on the dev box. **Bounded, acknowledged gap:** TRUE non-coherent-hardware validation (where a dropped invalidate genuinely corrupts) requires **EB.1 cross-vendor CI (AMD/Intel)**, which is **OUT of M3.0 scope**. M3.0 proves code-path execution + byte-exact equality on coherent hardware; EB.1 proves non-coherent semantics on real hardware.

### VK_KHR_buffer_device_address — deferred to M3.1; VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement — out of scope
BDA would change the **shader** (descriptor-bound SSBO -> 64-bit `PhysicalStorageBuffer` pointer, requiring `PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses`, codegen, and a `@target` declaration), violating M3.0's no-codegen invariant, and it does not address the M3.0 bottleneck. Deferred to M3.1 (tiled matmul + cooperative_matrix), which already touches codegen. **VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement** (import-host-pointer) is consciously scoped OUT in favor of the HOST_CACHED ladder, which reaches the gate; revisit only if a target vendor lacks HOST_CACHED.

### Acceptance gates
- `dispatch_saxpy_1m` < **1 ms** and `dispatch_q4km_512` < **2 ms** on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (bench IDs unchanged).
- All existing dispatch + Q4_K_M bit-exact tests pass; the four force-option paths (AT-1418) produce byte-identical output.
- Lavapipe single-queue fallback shows no regression; `cargo test --workspace` (+`--ignored`) green; `clippy -D warnings` clean; `spirv-val` clean.

### New/changed error variants
`DispatchError` grows to 28 variants: `SemaphoreCreationFailed`, `TransferQueueSubmitFailed`, and `MappedRangeOpFailed { op: MappedRangeOp }` (`MappedRangeOp in {Flush, Invalidate}`).
qa_handoff: AT-1400/AT-1401 (perf gates) are measured ONLY on the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 dev machine; CI (Lavapipe) CANNOT validate the 1 ms/2 ms gates. QA must mark these NOT-EXERCISED (not BLOCKED, not FAILED) on a CI-only run, and record the dev-machine medians separately. All correctness ATs (1402-1420) run in CI on Lavapipe single-queue coherent; AT-1409/AT-1413/AT-1414/AT-1418 additionally require AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS=1 and exercise the dedicated/binary/non-coherent CODE paths via force-options even on coherent hardware (byte-exact oracle holds). TRUE non-coherent + multi-queue HARDWARE validation is EB.1 (AMD/Intel), out of M3.0 scope.
